subject: PacerHealth: operator orchestration & secrets escrow — BYOK scope review
messages:
From: Anika Singh <anika@pacerhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: PacerHealth Security <security@pacerhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial scope: BYOK, HSM placement & escrow expectations

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — I'm Anika (CTO, PacerHealth). We're evaluating Redwood Private for a PHI-handling workload and have a few hard requirements around key custody and operator separation before we can proceed to procurement. High level:

- We require customer-controlled KEKs (BYOK).
- HSM must be attested and either physically located in our VPC/on-prem or under a strict escrow model we can audit.
- Operators (on both sides) must be separated; we need an operator orchestration model that prevents unilateral key unwrapping.
- Rotation/rolling procedures need to support emergency re-wrap and verifiable audit trails (immutable logs + signed attestations).

I've attached a short requirements doc (pacer_kms_requirements_v1.pdf) that lays out our compliance asks (SOC2/HIPAA controls mapped). Could you confirm whether Redwood supports: KMIP vs PKCS#11, an offline HSM-escrow handshake, blind signing / non-extractable keys, and automated rotation windows tied to commit policies?

We'd like to run a short 30–45 min technical scoping call next week with your solutions engineer and our security lead. Proposed slots: Tue 4/13 10–11am PT or Wed 4/14 2–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Anika
CTO, PacerHealth

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear requirements and the doc. Putting a short reply here to align on next steps and call out immediate clarifications so we can prepare the right ops/arch artifacts for the call.

Quick answers up-front:
- Redwood Private supports BYOK via customer-supplied KEKs. We support both remote wrap (customer HSM wrapping a KEK) and an HSM-in-customer-network pattern where the HSM is reachable over private links.
- We have production integrations with both KMIP and PKCS#11-based HSMs; KMIP is our recommended route for networked module management.
- We can provide an escrow / sealed-key workflow that includes split custody (operator shards + customer escrow), signed audit attestations, and an attestation snapshot for each rotation event.
- Blind signing (non-extractable keys) is supported at the wrapper level if the HSM supports those semantics; we'll need exact model/firmware details to confirm.

For the call we'd like to propose an internal agenda:
1) Clarify HSM placement preference (customer-onprem vs. vendor-provided in their network)
2) Confirm KMIP vs PKCS#11 model and whether you have specific HSM vendors in scope (Thales, Entrust, AWS CloudHSM, etc.)
3) Review operator orchestration: how many operator roles, emergency unseal flow, escrow unlocking ceremony
4) Audit/attestation formats and log forwarding (syslog/immutable blob store)

I can do Tue 4/13 10:00–10:45am PT. aditya and Grace will join to cover runtime and ops.

I'll attach a short draft proposal (redwood-byok-proposal-draft-v1.docx) after we confirm the call time — it will include a sample topology (VPC peering, private link, operator jumpbox segmentation) and a suggested rotation cadence default (90 days with emergency 7-day rewrap).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial scope: BYOK, HSM placement & escrow expectations

Anika — quick tech notes from runtime/serving perspective so we can scope integration effort and call artifacts.

1) HSM placement patterns we support (summary):
   - Customer-hosted HSM in their VPC/on-prem (Redwood talks KMIP over private link; KMS agent runs in customer subnet).
   - Customer-provided HSM in colocation with an encrypted control plane link (for air-gapped requirements we provide an escrow handshake tool).
   - Redwood-managed HSM in a dedicated tenant network with split-custody escrow for sensitive keys.

2) Protocols: we have production KMIP adapters and a PKCS#11 shim for older modules. KMIP gives better lifecycle control for rotation and remote rewrap.

3) Attack surface & operator separation: recommend operator orchestration using a 2-person ceremony for emergency unseal + HSM attestation snapshots signed with a separate root-of-trust. We also support ephemeral wrapping keys for session-level usage to avoid exposing master KEKs during normal operation.

4) Rotation automation: our operator toolkit supports scheduled rotation workflows (cron-based) and manual emergency rewrap. For your compliance ask, we can ship immutable attestations to your SIEM / S3 retention bucket with signed metadata including HSM attestation quote (vendor-dependent).

Questions for Pacer ahead of the call:
- Do you require on-prem HSM hardware (FIPS/HSM in your data center) or is a HSM in your cloud VPC acceptable?
- Are you able to run a small KMS agent on a VM in your network for KMIP connectivity?
- Do you have a preferred key lifecycle frequency? (e.g., master KEK rotation every 1 year, DEK every 90 days)

If you can confirm preferences we will tailor the draft architecture.

- Aditya (Infra Lead, Redwood Inference)
From: Anika Singh <anika@pacerhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@pacerhealth.com, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial scope: BYOK, HSM placement & escrow expectations

Mina/Aditya — thanks for the quick notes. A few clarifications from our security team: we require the HSM to be physically controlled by Pacer (customer-owned) inside our VPC for our initial rollout. That means we will provision a validated FIPS 140-2/3 module (likely Thales or Gemalto hardware) accessible over our private network.

Answers:
- On-prem/cloud: on-prem / VPC-local HSM only for now.
- KMIP agent: yes, we can host an agent VM for KMIP connectivity.
- Key rotation cadence: we are asking for master KEK rotation annually, DEK rotation 90 days, with the ability to trigger emergency rewrap immediately and generate a signed attestation.
- Audit forwarding: we prefer logs pushed to our SIEM (Splunk) and retain attestations for a minimum of 7 years.

We also want to see a sample operator ceremony runbook and the expected roles/permissions matrix ahead of procurement. Please include: the unseal ceremony steps, the minimal operator privileges, and the rollback plan if a rotation fails.

I'll lock the call for Tue 4/13 10:00am PT. Attendees: myself, Tom Li (security), and Rachel M. (infrastructure).

Thanks — Anika
